headline: QatarEnergy Extends LNG Force Majeure Through 2026
summary: QatarEnergy extended a force majeure on LNG deliveries to the end of 2026, leaving Europe and Asia without certain term supplies. The extension drove European natural gas prices to their highest level since autumn 2022.
why: QatarEnergy is Qatar's state-owned petroleum company and one of the world's largest exporters of liquefied natural gas. Prolonged supply disruptions significantly impact global energy markets and European power generation costs.

impacts.name: European Utilities
impacts.why: Higher natural gas import costs squeeze profit margins for European power and gas providers.

why_moved: QatarEnergy's force majeure extension cuts committed LNG supplies to Europe and Asia through 2026, triggering a sharp surge in European natural gas benchmark prices.
